# User guide: The Notebook

## In plain words

The Notebook is a place where your agents leave things for you to read, tick, answer and keep. An agent writes to the terminal for short answers. It writes to the Notebook for anything that you must follow, compare or decide. Examples are a test script, a design, a decision or a login for an app under test. The terminal scrolls away, but a note stays where you put it. You can read, edit, comment on and answer every note. Each project has its own Notebook, and notes are plain files that git can keep.

## Where to find it

- **The terminal page.** A small tab with a book icon sits on the right edge of the page. Press it to open the Notebook drawer. You can also press Ctrl+Shift+N. Drag the tab up or down to move it. The tab remembers its place.
- **Under the book icon.** The tab has more parts: a pin, a magnifier (**Search the Notebook**) and a plus (**New**). A red dot on the book icon means that a note needs your attention.
- **A phone.** The drawer fills the screen. The tab is short. Press the three dots on the tab to show the search and plus parts for a few seconds.
- **The wide list.** Drag the left edge of the drawer to make it wider. From 640 pixels the list of notes sits beside the open note.
- **A note in its own browser tab.** Choose **Open in new tab** on a note. The note opens full size on its own page with a **Back to Notebook** link.
- **The wiki.** The **Wiki** button in the drawer header opens the wiki view. See [The wiki](wiki.md).
- **Settings.** The **Notebook** card on the **Configuration** tab of the plugin settings holds the Notebook settings.

The Notebook needs a workspace that has a project folder. A workspace without a project folder shows "The Notebook is not available here". The **Global** switch then offers a Notebook that belongs to no project.

## How to use it

### Open and close the drawer

1. Press the book tab. Expect: the drawer slides in from the right.
2. Press the book tab again, press Escape, or press the **Close the Notebook** button. Expect: an unpinned drawer slides out.
3. Press the pin on the tab to pin the drawer. Expect: the terminal gets narrower and the drawer stays beside it. The pinned drawer shows a row of icons at the top: **Unpin**, **Wiki**, **Search the Notebook** and **New**.

A click outside an unpinned drawer closes it. The drawer refuses to pin when the window is too narrow, and it says so. Drag the left edge of the drawer to change its width. The width is kept for each workspace.

The header has a **Project** and **Global** switch. **Project** shows the Notebook in the project folder of the workspace. **Global** shows notes that belong to no project. The Global Notebook lives on the Unraid flash drive and is never committed to git.

### The list and the four areas

The list shows one line for each note: a type icon, the title, who made it and when, and small marks on the right. The list has four areas. Each area has a count. Press an area name to open or close it.

| Area | What it holds |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Inbox** | New things from agents, for you to look at. An agent puts a note here unless it names another area. |
| **Working** | Work in progress, such as the scratch notes of an agent. |
| **Notes** | Notes that you keep. |
| **Voice mail** | The spoken messages that agents copy into the Notebook. It sits after **Notes** and before **Archive**. See below. |
| **Archive** | Notes that are put away. The Archive never deletes by itself. |

**Voice mail** is closed at first, so spoken messages do not bury your notes. Its count shows how many are new, for example "Voice mail · 3 new". With none new, it shows the total. Press the heading, or press Enter or Space on it, to open or close it. The Notebook remembers your choice in this browser. A spoken message that you move to the **Archive** shows under **Archive**. A search that finds a spoken message opens the heading.

Pinned notes stay at the top of their area. The rest are sorted by the time of the last change.

### What moves a note between areas

Nothing moves a note on its own. A note moves only when someone acts.

- You choose **Move to** in the menu of a note. The menu offers each area except the one that holds the note and the Archive.
- An agent moves a note with its Notebook tools.
- **Archive** moves a note to the Archive. **Restore to Notes** moves it back to the **Notes** area.
- **Delete** moves a note to the Archive after a short delay. See the section on quick delete below.

A note that another workspace shares with you lands in your **Inbox**.

### Make a note

1. Press **New** in the list (or the plus on the tab). Expect: a menu opens.
2. Choose a type under **New**, or a template under **From a template**. Expect: the Notebook makes the note and opens it in a tab. A note made from a type has its title ready to rename.
3. Type the title and press Enter.
4. Press **Edit in the editor** to write the content. The file editor opens on the file of the note.

The command palette also makes notes. Press Ctrl+K, or press the slash key while the drawer has focus. Type "New" and choose a type. Type "New from template" for a template.

### Note types

The type of a note decides how the Notebook shows it. An agent chooses the type when it makes the note.

| Type (label) | What it shows |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Note** | Markdown text (plain text with simple marks for headings, lists and links). A note can link to another note with its title in double square brackets. |
| **Checklist** | Steps with a result for each: pass, fail, blocked or skip. A bar shows the progress. **Next step** jumps to the next step with no result. |
| **Connection** | A card for an app: addresses, a user name and secrets. See the section on secrets below. |
| **Question** | A card with questions for you and one **Submit** button. |
| **Slides** | Slides with speaker notes, with previous and next buttons and a print option. |
| **Diagram** | A Mermaid diagram (a diagram that is written as text). |
| **Drawing** | An SVG picture. |
| **Page** | A web page. It opens with its scripts off. See "A page with scripts" below. |
| **Table**, **Chart**, **Status** | Rows and columns, a chart, or a set of status tiles. |
| **Log**, **Diff**, **Data** | Plain log lines, a unified diff, or JSON data. |
| **Board** | Columns of cards. You can move, edit and delete cards. |
| **Walkthrough** | A tour through places in your code, one stop at a time. |
| **Media** | Images, video, audio or PDF files from the assets folder. |
| **Web preview** | A preview of a running web app. |
| **Progress** | A live progress card for a long job. |

### Templates

A template is a note that is already half written. The **New** menu lists each template with a short description.

| Template | Type | What it is for |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Manual test plan** | Checklist | Steps to check a change by hand, with the expected result for each step. |
| **Release checklist** | Checklist | What to confirm before, during and after a release. |
| **User acceptance test script** | Checklist | Scenarios that a business user runs to accept a change. |
| **Deployment runbook** | Checklist | Exact steps to deploy a service, with a check after each step and the way back. |
| **Onboarding guide** | Checklist | A checklist for a new person: access, tools, first tasks and people to meet. |
| **Incident report** | Note | What happened, who was affected, why, and what changes. |
| **Design review** | Note | A design proposal with the problem, the options, the risks and the questions. |
| **Decision record** | Note | One decision: the context, the options, the choice and what follows. |
| **Status report** | Note | A short report for a period. |
| **Handover note** | Note | Everything the next person needs to carry on. |
| **Bug report** | Note | A fault that someone else can reproduce. |
| **Meeting notes** | Note | Who came, what was decided, and who does what by when. |
| **API reference** | Note | The address, the sign-in, each call and the errors. |

The menu also lists starting pages for the wiki (such as **Wiki home**, **Runbooks** and **Glossary**). See [The wiki](wiki.md).

### Read and work with a note

An open note has a header with the title and a row of icon buttons. A line below the title shows a flag (when the note needs you, or is New or Changed), the time of the last update, and **Not committed** when the file differs from the last git commit.

- Double-click the title to rename it. **Rename...** in the **More actions** menu does the same.
- **Edit in the editor** opens the file of the note in the file editor. If an agent changes the note while the editor is open, Save does not replace the change. The editor keeps your text, says who changed the note, and offers **Copy my text** and **Reload**.
- The star pins the note to the top of its area. See "Pins" below.
- **Open in new tab** opens the note on its own page.
- The button with the notebook and three small stars (**Ask the agent to refresh this note**) shows at every drawer width.
- **Read aloud**, **History**, **Go to comments** and **Properties** show as icons when the drawer is wide (760 pixels or more). In a narrower drawer they move into the **More actions** menu.
- **More actions** also holds **Copy link**, **Move to**, **Share a copy to**, **Export**, **Lock** and **Archive**.

Several open notes show as tabs above the note. A tab that does not fit goes into an "N more" menu. Press the cross on a tab, or press the middle mouse button, to close it. Alt+] and Alt+[ step to the next and the previous tab. A screen reader reads the tabs as a group of buttons, and the open note is marked as current. On a phone each tab, its cross and the **All notes** button have a touch area of 44 pixels. When you open a note with the Enter key, the keyboard stays in the drawer, so Ctrl+K, Alt+[ and Alt+] keep working.

### Go back to the note you came from

When you follow a link inside a note (a link in **Linked from**, a wiki link written with double square brackets, or a click in a diagram), the target opens as a new active tab. The drawer remembers the note you left. Two buttons then show at the start of the note header: **Back to** (the title of the note you left) and **Forward to** (after a Back). A button that has nowhere to go is dimmed. Alt+Left does the same as Back and Alt+Right does the same as Forward. The keys do nothing while you type in a field. A link that you follow after a Back removes Forward, as in a browser. A note that you open from the list, the search or a tab is not a link, so it does not add a step. The drawer keeps this history in memory only: a reload clears it. On a phone each button has a touch area of 44 pixels.

In a wide drawer the list hides while a note is open, so the note gets the full width. Press **Show note list** (or **Hide note list**) to change that. The choice is kept for each workspace. In a narrow drawer the list is a tab of its own (the list icon, **All notes**).

### The Properties panel

Press **Properties** (the "i" icon) to see the facts that the header leaves out.

| Row | What it shows |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Type**, **Area** | The type and the area of the note. |
| **Made by**, **Edited by** | The person or agent who made the note. **Edited by** says if you, an agent or both changed it. |
| **Created**, **Updated** | The full date and time. |
| **File path** | The path of the file in the notebook folder. |
| **Id**, **Version** | The id of the note and a short code that changes with every change of the file. |
| **Tags** | The tags of the note. In the Notes list, press a tag to filter the list. |

**Copy id** and **Copy path** copy the value. **Linked from (N)** lists the pages that link to this note. Press a name to open that page. Press Escape to close the panel.

### Comments and the "needs you" flag

Each note has a **Comments** section at the bottom. It starts closed. A chip shows how many comments are open.

1. Open **Comments**.
2. Type in the box and press **Send**. Ctrl+Enter also sends.
3. Press **Reply** under a comment to answer it. Press the tick to resolve it. Press **Show N resolved** to see resolved comments again.

A comment can point at the whole file, a section, a checklist step, a diagram node, a line, a walkthrough stop or a slide. A step of a checklist has its own comment box.

A note is marked **Needs you** when one of these is true:

- An agent marked the note as waiting for you.
- The note is a **Question** card that nobody has answered.
- An agent left a comment that is not resolved.

A **Needs you** note stays marked until you answer the card or resolve the comment. Opening the note does not clear the mark. An archived note has no mark and its comments are read-only.

### Marks and badges

| Mark | Where | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Red dot on the book tab | The edge of the page | At least one note or wiki page needs your attention: it needs you, it is New or it is Changed. The dot has no number. Its screen-reader name has the count. |
| Number on the **Wiki** button | The drawer header | The count of wiki pages that need your attention. Notes of the Notes world do not count here. |
| Alert icon | A list row, a tab | **Needs you**. |
| Dot | A list row, a tab | **New** (you have not seen the note) or **Changed** (it changed after you last saw it). |
| Star | A list row | The note is pinned. |
| Lock | A list row | A person locked the note. See "Lock a note". |
| **Journal** chip | A list row | The note is the Agent journal. |
| Dashed circle | A list row | **Not committed**. |

When an agent adds or changes a note, a glow runs round the row and the closed tab. A label slides out beside the tab for a few seconds, such as "Plug added a note". A banner under the header says what changed and has an **Open** button. A note that is open for about a second and a half counts as read.

If the setting **Open the Notebook when an agent asks** is on, the drawer opens by itself for a note that an agent asks to show. When the drawer is open and an agent adds a **Question** card or a note that needs you, the Notebook opens that note in a tab. The Activity tray shows a line for every note change that an agent makes. The line has an **Open note** button. It opens the workspace and then the note.

### Questions and answers

A **Question** card asks for a choice, several choices, yes or no, approve or reject, or a text, number or date. Choose your answers and press **Submit**. Expect: the card shows "Answered". When the setting **Tell the agent when I answer** is on, the Notebook types one short line into the terminal of the workspace. The line names the card. It never holds your answer. The agent reads the answer from the card.

The same setting covers four more actions. The Notebook tells the agent when you finish a checklist, mark a step as failed, add a comment, or save a login on a connection card. A busy agent is not interrupted. The Notebook then says that the answer is saved and that you must tell the agent to read it. Nothing is queued.

### Pins

The star on a note, and **Pin to the top** in its menu, keep the note at the top of its area. This pin is not the pin on the tab. The pin on the tab fixes the whole drawer beside the terminal.

### Lock a note

**More actions**, **Lock: agents may only comment** locks a note. An agent can then add comments but cannot change the note. You can still edit a locked note. **Unlock** gives the note back to the agents.

### Delete, Archive and the Archive rule

Each row has a bin icon and a menu with **Archive** and **Delete**.

1. Press the bin, or choose **Delete** in the menu. Expect: the note leaves the list at once. A pill at the bottom of the Notebook says what will happen and shows **Undo**.
2. Press **Undo** within 8 seconds to bring the note back. Nothing changes on disk.
3. Wait for the pill to end. Expect: a note in **Inbox**, **Working** or **Notes** moves to the **Archive**. A note that is already in the **Archive** is removed for good.

> [!WARNING]
> A note that you delete from the **Archive** is gone for good. The Notebook removes the file, its comments and its stored secrets. Git keeps older commits of the file, but the Notebook cannot bring it back.

Several deletes in a row share one pill, such as "3 notes deleted". If you close the Notebook before the pill ends, a move to the **Archive** still happens, but a removal for good does not. The note then stays.

Only a person can remove a note for good. An agent cannot. An agent can only ask, and you approve the request in the Activity tray. An archived note is read-only. Choose **Restore to Notes** to work on it again.

### Share a note to another workspace

1. Open the menu of a note (the three dots on a row, or **More actions**).
2. Open **Share a copy to**. The list shows each workspace that is open. It starts closed each time.
3. Choose a workspace. Expect: a short message says "Shared a copy".

The Notebook puts a copy in the **Inbox** of that project. The copy is not pinned and does not need you. A copy of a connection card does not carry its secrets. Enter them again on the copy. Sharing to the same project is refused.

### Secrets inside a note

Write no password, token or key in a note. The Notebook refuses to save text from an agent that looks like a secret. Put a secret on a **Connection** card instead.

A connection card keeps a list of addresses, a user name, and up to three secrets: **Password**, **Token** and **API key**. The card file holds only a reference. The value is in the encrypted vault (the plugin's store for secrets). The value is not in the file, in git, in search, in an export, in the Activity tray or in voice mail.

- A secret shows as a row of dots.
- Press the eye to reveal it. It hides again after 15 seconds and a countdown shows the time left.
- Press **Copy the password without showing it** to copy it. The Notebook offers **Clear clipboard** after the copy.
- Press **Set**, or **Change** in the menu, to enter a value. Press **Clear** to remove it from the vault. The Notebook asks you to confirm.
- Press the pulse icon (**Check that ... is up**) next to an address. The card shows the status code and the time. The check works only for addresses on your local network.
- An agent can set a secret but cannot read one back.

The setting **Production keys on connection cards** is **Refuse** by default. With **Refuse**, the vault turns away a value that looks like a live production key. A connection card in the **Global** Notebook cannot hold a secret.

The vault lives on this Unraid server. If you move the notebook folder to another server, the card moves but the secrets do not. The card then says "secret not on this server - enter it again".

### A page with scripts

A **Page** note opens with its scripts off. A banner says "Scripts are off for this page". Press **Run scripts** to let that one page run its scripts. Press **Stop this page** to turn them off again. The choice is not kept. A page that runs scripts still has no network, no storage and no way to reach the rest of the Unraid page. A page that tries to leave the note is removed. Press **Reload** to show it again.

### Read aloud

Press **Read aloud** (the speaker icon) to hear the whole note. The Notebook cuts the note into short pieces of sentences and plays them one after the other.

1. Press **Read aloud**. Expect: a ring spins while the first piece is made, then a wave shows while sound plays.
2. Press the button again to pause. Press it a third time to continue. Press it while the ring spins to cancel.
3. Press Escape while the button has focus, close the note or change to another note to stop the reading.

Read aloud needs the global voice switch to be on. See [Voice](voice.md). It uses the voice and the speed of the workspace. The mute switch of the workspace does not apply, because you asked for the reading. A message that a workspace speaks never plays on top of the reading. The message waits for the end of the sentence that plays. If a note changes while it is read, the reading stops with a message.

### Ask the agent to update a note

A note can go stale while the agent keeps working. Press the button with the notebook and three small stars (**Ask the agent to refresh this note**). The Notebook types one line into the terminal of the workspace. The line names the note by title, file path and id. It asks the agent to read the note again, update it and save the answer in the Notebook.

The button then tells you what happened:

- **Asked. The agent has the note path.** The line was typed.
- **The agent is busy, nothing was typed.** Nothing is queued. Press the button again when the agent waits at its prompt.
- **The request was refused.** A message gives the reason, such as a workspace that does not run.

The button says only that the agent was asked. It does not say that the note is updated. The button is hidden in the **Global** Notebook, because that Notebook has no agent.

### Size limits

| Limit | Value |
| :-- | :-- |
| One note file | 1 MB. A save over the limit is refused with the message "This artefact is larger than 1 MB". |
| Notes in one notebook | 2,000. |
| One uploaded file (an asset) | 5 MB. |
| All assets of one notebook | 100 MB. |
| Changes by agents | 60 each minute for one notebook. You are never limited. |

Drag a file onto the open drawer to upload it as an asset. The Notebook shows the path to use in a note.

### Search and the command palette

- The search field at the top of the list filters the list by title, tag, summary, maker and type.
- From two characters, the Notebook also searches inside the notes. The matches show under the field with a short snippet. This search skips secrets.
- **Filters** (the sliders icon) filters by type, tag and maker. A dot on the button shows that a filter is on. **Clear filters** removes them all.
- Ctrl+K (or the slash key) opens the command palette. It opens a note, makes a note from a type or a template, or jumps to an area with "Go to Inbox". Arrow keys move, Enter runs and Escape closes.

### The git history of a note

Press **History** to see the git history of the open note. The panel shows:

- **Committed** or **Not committed**.
- The last commits that touched the file, with a short hash, the subject, the author and the time.
- The changes since the last commit.
- A `git checkout` command that you can copy to bring back the last committed text. Run it in a terminal. It replaces the file.

If the project folder is not inside a git repository, the panel says so and suggests `git init`. The Notebook keeps no history of its own. Git is the history. A change that was never committed cannot be brought back.

### Import and export

The **More** menu in the drawer header holds these items:

- **Import...** takes a Markdown file or a zip of notes. A zip keeps the ids of the notes. A note with an id that is already there is skipped.
- **This note as Markdown** and **This note as a web page** export the open note.
- **Inbox as a zip**, **Working as a zip**, **Notes as a zip** and **Archive as a zip** export one area.
- **Notebook settings** opens the Notebook card in the plugin settings.

### The Journal

The setting **Agent journal** is **Off** by default. When it is **On**, an agent can add short lines about what it did and why to a note called **Agent journal** in the **Working** area. The list marks that note with a **Journal** chip. Each line has a time and the name of the agent. The note keeps the newest 500 lines. Older lines move to monthly notes in the **Archive**. Nothing is deleted. A person reads the journal like any note. A locked journal refuses agents.

## Choices and settings

These settings are on the **Configuration** tab, in the **Notebook** card. Only a person can change them. An agent cannot.

| Setting | What it does | Default | When to change it |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Notebook** | Shows or hides the Notebook drawer and the agent tools. **Off** hides the drawer and refuses the tools. Nothing is deleted. You do not need **Let agents manage the plugin** for agents to use the Notebook. | On | Turn it off when you do not want agents to use a Notebook. Reload the page after the change. |
| **Show the Wiki page** | Adds a **Wiki** item to the Tasks menu. | Off | Turn it on to read the wiki without a terminal. See [The wiki](wiki.md). |
| **Open the Notebook when an agent asks** | Opens the drawer when an agent adds a note and asks to show it. | No | Turn it on when you want to see notes at once. With **No**, the tab shows a dot only. |
| **Folder name** | The folder in each project that holds the notebook. Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore. Up to 40 characters. | notebook | Change it only before you use the Notebook. A change does not move an existing notebook. |
| **Production keys on connection cards** | Lets a card hold a value that looks like a live production key. | Refuse | Allow it only when you really store a production key. |
| **Tell the agent when I answer** | Types one short line into the terminal when you answer a card, finish a checklist, fail a step, comment or save a login. | Yes | Turn it off when you prefer to tell the agent yourself. |
| **Speak a notice when a page waits for me** | Speaks one short sentence when an agent adds a note that waits for you. Needs agent voice to be on. | No | Turn it on when you work away from the screen. |
| **Quiet hours** | A time window, such as 22:00-07:00, in the server's local time. No Notebook notice is spoken in it. The window may cross midnight. | Empty | Set it when you do not want notices at night. |
| **Agent journal** | Lets agents add lines to the Agent journal note. | Off | Turn it on when you want a timeline of what agents did. |

## What happens behind the scenes

A notebook is a folder called notebook in the root of the project. It holds one folder for each area and one plain file for each note. Git can keep the folder, and a second workspace on the same project shares the same notebook. The drawer shows a change of an agent without a reload. The drawer is part of the terminal app. See C4 Component: React Terminal Spa and C4 Component: Server Rendered Ui.

## If something goes wrong

| What you see | What it means | What to do |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| "The Notebook is not available here" | The workspace has no project folder. | Use the **Global** Notebook, or give the workspace a project folder. |
| No book tab on the page | The setting **Notebook** is **Off**, or the page was not reloaded after you turned it on. | Turn the setting on and reload the page. |
| "The Notebook is turned off in the plugin settings." | An agent tool or the page tried to use a Notebook that is off. | Turn on **Notebook** in the plugin settings. |
| A change is refused because the note changed | You and an agent changed the same note at the same time. The Notebook protects the newer text. | Read the note again, then redo your change. |
| "This artefact is larger than 1 MB" | The note is over the size limit. | Split the note in two. |
| "Not committed" on a note | The file differs from the last git commit. | Commit the notebook folder with git. |
| **Read aloud** says the voice is off | The global voice switch is off. | Turn on voice. See [Voice](voice.md). |
| Refresh says "The agent is busy" | The agent is not at its prompt. | Wait until the agent waits for input, then press the button again. |
| A secret says "not on this server" | The card came from another server. | Press **Set** and enter the secret again. |
| A **Page** note shows no script | Scripts are off by design. | Press **Run scripts** if you trust the page. |
| The drawer will not pin | The window is too narrow. | Make the window wider, or leave the drawer unpinned. |
